title: The Answer Was on Top
thesis_this_serves: An answer that repeats for every searcher sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text was underneath. The look has to make DEPTH the argument: top is bright and easy, bottom is dark and binding, and the camera earns the descent.

roles.sky: #A9B7C0  Kodiak slate fog, cold blue-grey overcast, the marsh at 7am
roles.ground: #2B211A  wet peat umber, the binder and the marsh floor, the dark anchor
roles.hero: #E8590C  hunter orange, ONE MEANING ONLY: the repeated wrong answer (the answer card and its twin). It never marks the binder
roles.accent: #8C9A86  lichen grey-green, desaturated sedge on the marsh only
roles.paper: #ECEEEA  cool grey-white summary stock, never warm bone
roles.rim: #EDF1F3  cool white, the rim on every sheet edge, hand silhouette and the corrected/blank tag

palette.mood: Cold, quiet, damp and fair. Nobody is scolded. The only warm saturated thing in a slate world is the wrong answer, so orange reads as a warning without a red alarm. A dim desaturated lamp pool (#D9B37A at 30 percent) lights the kitchen table but NEVER lights an orange object directly. When the tag reaches the binder it turns blank paper on peat so the move reads as the answer being corrected, never as the binder being marked wrong.
palette.divergence: Measured against the last ten films. 2026-09-23 was dusk violet #3E3852, birch gold #C9A227, copper #C87137 and carbon #1F3A5F. 2026-09-19 was powerhouse green with sodium amber and cyan. 2026-08-05 was cabinet green #1E332C, bone #EDE7DA and brass #C9963F. This film has no green ground, no violet, no gold, no brass, no copper, no cyan, and no warm-bone paper: slate fog #A9B7C0, peat umber #2B211A, cool paper #ECEEEA. Its only warm role is hunter orange, which none of the last ten used as a hero role. Orange has one semantic job.

light.time_of_day: 07:10, September 5th and after, Kodiak. Sun not yet over the ridge, then indoor lamp and phone glow for the rest.
light.direction: soft overcast from above for the marsh; a single warm lamp from frame RIGHT on the kitchen table; the phone glass lights hands from below
light.key: per setup; nothing is lit by an unnamed source
light.rim: cool white #EDF1F3 on every sheet edge and hand silhouette
light.depth_approach: Four summary layers plus one binder in the S12 dive, at a declared 3/4 oblique camera (yaw 18, pitch 24). t=0 table (focusZ on plane 1, then focusZ animates to the binder, which is pinned in focus): plane 1 the orange AnswerCard on a paper backer #ECEEEA L93 blur 0 shadow +6/+10; plane 2 Google's help page #DCE0E1 L88 blur 0.6 shadow +5/+8; plane 3 the ADF&G page #C8CED1 L82 blur 1.4 shadow +4/+6; plane 4 the Public Safety card #B0B8BD L74 blur 2.4 shadow +3/+5; binder #2B211A L15 pinned blur 0 with a hard 1px contact shadow, rounded spine, stitched head band and page-block edge. Sheets are 8 to 12 percent translucent over a paper underlay. Exterior table: far ridge #8797A1 at 18 percent contrast, mid marsh #6F7C6C at 100, near alder #2B211A at 130 with slight blur. Blur is derived from lib/focus.ts blurAt(z, focusZ, aperture, sharp, max, pinned).

shape_language.grammar: THE THIN, LIGHT SUMMARY AGAINST THE THICK, DARK BINDING TEXT.
shape_language.why_this_story: The argument is about layers. So every summary is a thin translucent pale rectangle that floats and wobbles, and the binding regulation is a thick, matte, peat-dark block with a spine and page edge, heavy and still. Natural forms (marsh grass, fog, snipe silhouettes) are irregular. The stack never blends with them, it lies over the land like a document does.
shape_language.the_deliberate_contrast: Thin pale floaty rectangles against one thick dark still block. Not a document layout: the camera travels through the sheets like a core sample.
shape_language.binder_wins_at_feed_scale: The binder carries a SECOND contrast axis beyond value: a rounded spine, a stitched head band, a page-block edge and a hard contact shadow, all at the 3/4 camera tilt, where sheets get only a soft float shadow. A 0.28-scale legibility strip is run on S1 and S12 before any other scene is authored.

casting.hero_reason: The story's real subject is the one thick still text underneath, and no bound thick block exists on the shelf. NET-NEW in lib/stack.tsx: Binder (thick peat umber block with rounded spine, stitched head band, page-block edge, hard contact shadow, opens via open 0..1 to a page), DateTag (the orange throughline tab with state orange or blank paper, tear and crease), AnswerCard (the orange card and its lockstep twin), LabelSheet (a thin summary sheet) and HandSil (silhouette hands, Weaver is never drawn with a face). The stack of summaries is a THIN composite of LabelSheets and is not the hero. It appears in ONE shot only (S12, the dive). Hero differs from the last two, Statement and RunOfRiver.
from_the_shelf: paper.tsx PaperFiber and the Sheet body/shadow contract as the reference for LabelSheet
credentials.tsx QuestionToken as the engraving pattern reference for DateTag
casting.cast_freshness: hero Binder differs from the last two heroes.

motion_language.how_the_world_moves: Everything thin wobbles on a spring. The binder is still. The camera makes one continuous descent, the S12 dive; every other shot is its own composed world.
key_hero_moves: the orange answer card slams onto the phone glass with overshoot
the twin card clacks down in perfect sync with the first, a mirrored bounce
the tag tears at its crease and slides away with the phone, leaving its torn corner
the S12 dive: the camera passes four layers about a second each, each a miniature of an earlier world, while the tag falls away and lands blank on the binder
the viewer's hands turn the binder page toward camera at the kitchen table
motion_language.blur_anticipation: 180 degree shutter on the slam and the peel; anticipation of about 3 frames before every stamp

composition.staging: 9:16 master graded; the square is derived at y 420 to 1500. Story band 500 to 1300, captions own 1336 to 1472. Sheets fill above and below the crop.
composition.focal_hierarchy: one card or tag at frame center at every key moment; the stack is the background structure
composition.negative_space: fog above the marsh; black phone glass in the hook
composition.signature_shot: S12: four summary sheets, each a miniature of an earlier world (the orange AI answer card, Google's help page, the ADF&G page stamped A SUMMARY, the Public Safety card), fall over one thick still peat binder at a 3/4 camera. The orange card holds on top as the VO says the answer was on top, then the camera DIVES down through the layers at about a second each while the tag falls off the top and lands blank on the binder cover, where the emergency-order slip lies in the binder's own family. The dive is the film's one continuous descent.

craft_advance.how: lib/focus.ts: blurAt(z, focusZ, aperture, sharp, max, pinned), valueLadder, passAlpha and perspScale as pure functions with a node self-test (scripts/focus_check.mjs), so a layered scene derives per-plane blur and value from its Z distance to a focal plane that can animate, with a pinned plane (the binder) always in focus. Registered under Engine systems in ASSET_MANIFEST.md.
